absent: Full layouts and lifecycles of direct I/O control, submit state, buffer head, page, iterator, kiocb and inode objects beyond fields touched here.
Mapping, bio allocation and attachment, page pinning, cleanup, await and complete helpers referenced but not routed.
Superblock lock and passive reference primitives, global list insertion and removal, and exclusive versus shared semantics.
Slab reclaim, LRU drain, mapping invalidation, writeback wait, workqueue setup and VM event accounting internals.
Eventfd creation, file operations table, userspace read and write paths, identifier allocator limits and flag value assignments.
Numeric values of operation flags, lock flags, poll masks, control modes, semaphore option and errno constants.
Error propagation and partial transfer accounting for mapping failures, allocation failures and I/O errors beyond the shown branches.

findings.text: Top level direct I/O entry accepts a kiocb, inode, optional block device, iterator, mapping callback, completion callback and flags, and returns transferred length, zero, negative errno or queued marker for async. It validates alignment, handles reads beyond sampled size, coordinates locking and page-cache writeback for locked reads, and drives mapping, submission, flush and completion phases.
Public superblock walk invokes a caller callback for each live superblock with an opaque argument, delegating to an internal walker with default flags that take shared superblock protection.
Kernel-side eventfd notification increments the counter with saturation and wakes pollers for input plus a caller supplied mask, while guarding against reentrant wakeup recursion.

Context holds a reference count, a wait queue head for sleepers, a 64-bit event counter, flag bits including semaphore behavior, and an integer identifier for allocator tracking. Counter updates occur under queue lock; reads for poll rely on ordering with queue insertion.

Deferred page flush preserves logical contiguity: if a bio is active and either the expected final block differs from the current page block or the current file offset differs from bio logical end, the active bio is submitted first. A missing bio triggers creation, and failure to attach the page triggers submit plus recreate with a single retry expected to succeed.

Page section submission accounts writes, coalesces an adjacent range on the same page when offset, length and block number are contiguous, otherwise flushes any deferred page and pins the new page with its offset, length, block and file offset. A boundary request forces immediate flush, bio submission and unpin of the deferred page.

Partial filesystem block zeroing runs once per mapping context and only when sub-block granularity is in use and the mapped buffer is newly allocated. It computes the leading or trailing uncovered sub-block count from position inside the filesystem block, submits that span from the shared zero page, and advances the next device block cursor.

Main direct I/O loop walks user pages and file blocks toward a final block. It acquires each page, derives per-page byte bounds from head and tail cursors, maps extents on demand, adjusts for sub-block remainder at start, handles unmapped holes by zero filling reads until aligned size or aborting writes for buffered fallback, optionally zeroes block starts, clamps each chunk by availability, page remainder and request remainder, propagates boundary hints, submits sections, and updates result and cursors with strict monotonic progress checks.

Reference release serializes decrement of the operation reference count under the operation bio lock with interrupt state saved, returning the remaining count so submitters and completers can decide atomically who performs final completion and wakeup.

Setup samples inode block bits, rejects misaligned offset and iterator alignment against filesystem then device granularity, returns zero for empty reads and reads starting at or beyond sampled size, optionally takes inode lock for locked reads and waits for overlapping page-cache writeback, forces synchronous mode for sync kiocb or extending writes, selects read or write operation flags, and prepares deferral resources for async dsync writes or racing buffered reads.

Teardown normalizes unmapped-write marker to zero for buffered fallback, zeroes trailing partial block span, flushes deferred page and active bio under a plug, releases pinned pages, drops read lock after lookups, returns queued marker only for successful async reads with data or fully completed async writes and otherwise waits, then completes and invalidates when the final reference drops.
Direct I/O entry records an in-flight operation by incrementing the inode direct I/O counter, paired with a later completion-side decrement not shown here.
Early initialization creates a dedicated slab cache for direct I/O control structures with panic on allocation failure and reports success.
Integer control storage holds the requested drop mask examined by the handler; only low bits select page-cache and slab work while a higher bit latches message suppression.

Page-cache dropper walks the superblock inode list under its list lock, takes each inode lock to skip freeing, will-free, new, or empty-and-not-needing-reschedule entries, grabs a reference before dropping both locks to invalidate the whole mapping range, releases the previous reference after each iteration, yields cooperatively, and drops the final reference at the end.

Control handler delegates parsing and range checks to a bounded integer vector helper, then on write drains reclaim locality and walks all superblocks to drop page cache when low bit set, drops reclaimable slab when next bit set, emits a one-time informational message with process identity and value, and latches suppression once the high bit appears.

Superblock iteration holds a global list lock while selecting first and next entries in requested direction, skips dying instances, acquires a passive reference that must succeed, drops the global lock before invoking the callback under shared or exclusive superblock lock unless unlocked iteration was requested, and defers release of the previous reference until after the next element is pinned.
Direction helpers select list ends or neighbors based on a reverse flag, returning head or tail as start and predecessor or successor as step, giving forward or reverse global superblock order.
Control table exposes a write-only integer named drop_caches backed by kernel storage, dispatched to the drop handler with bounds one through four.
Early initialization registers the drop caches control table under the virtual memory control directory and reports success.

Signaling holds the wait queue lock with interrupts saved, checks a per-task reentrancy flag and warns once on recursion, marks entry during update, performs saturating increment, wakes active pollers only when sleepers exist, clears the flag, then releases the lock.
Destruction releases the numeric identifier only when valid then frees the context via reference-count callback; file release wakes hangup pollers before dropping the context reference.

Poll registers the file on the context wait queue, then samples the counter once with ordering against queue insertion: positive count reports readable, maximum value reports error, and values below maximum minus one report writable.
Poll registration invokes the table queueing callback when present and then issues a full barrier that pairs with sleeper checks, preventing later readiness tests from moving before queue insertion.

Drain helper requires the queue lock held by the caller, returns one when semaphore mode is set and the counter is nonzero otherwise returns the full counter, and subtracts the returned amount from the stored counter.

Waiter removal holds the queue lock with interrupts saved while draining the counter, detaching the waiter, and waking writers when a nonzero amount was drained and sleepers remain, returning success on drained data and retry marker otherwise.

Direct I/O paths assert that retried page attachment succeeds, that computed chunk bytes are nonzero, that the file block cursor never passes the request end, and that queued status never appears before the final async decision point; violation indicates accounting or state machine corruption.

Counter saturates at the maximum 64-bit value rather than wrapping, poll reports both readable and error at saturation and suppresses writable near saturation, so producers must handle backpressure and consumers must drain to restore writability.
